criteria_notes.note: Not started. Nothing blocks wiring `max_body_size` into Starlette, Router, Mount and Route. I held off so the whole task can be re-planned together.

Blocked. Raising an outer limit from an inner Route, Mount or Router fails with the current middleware. The outer `receive_wrapper` (`body_limit.py:30-38`) checks `self.max_body_size`, a fixed value. It raises `HTTPException(413)` before the inner middleware sees the bytes, and the inner middleware can't reach the original `receive`. Lowering works, and so does the `Content-Length` fail-fast. Raising needs `receive_wrapper` to use the effective limit from `scope[MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY]` at call time. The inner middleware already writes that key, and the outer one has to read it back.
Not started. No files were changed, so the existing suite is unaffected.

replan_request.reason: Raising an outer limit from an inner Route, Mount or Router is impossible with the current RequestBodyLimitMiddleware. Its receive_wrapper compares the running total against self.max_body_size. The outer wrapper therefore raises 413 before an inner, higher limit can apply, and the inner middleware has no access to the original receive. The middleware needs to read the effective limit from scope[MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY] at receive time, which the inner middleware already sets. The Content-Length fail-fast should use the same effective limit. After that change, T3 can proceed in its own files.

summary: I stopped before making any edits. T3 can't meet ACC8 (an inner limit raising the outer one) with `RequestBodyLimitMiddleware` as T1 committed it, and the fix is in `starlette/middleware/body_limit.py`, which I'm not allowed to edit.
